input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle guard on the __cause__ walk was removed, so the loop now only terminates when the chain reaches an exception with no cause. A cyclic __cause__ chain would loop forever.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception whose __cause__ chain loops back on itself (e.g. a.__cause__ = b and b.__cause__ = a, which Python allows by manual assignment), raised inside a retried function with retry_if_exception_cause_type configured. Mechanism: the while condition at line 180 never sees exc become None or a seen object, so it spins indefinitely without advancing to a terminal state. Impact: the retry predicate hangs the calling thread instead of returning a decision.
critique: The finding describes the same defect: the __cause__ walk in retry_if_exception_cause_type has no cycle guard, so a cyclic cause chain loops forever and hangs the caller. The trigger (mutually causing exceptions), the mechanism (the loop never reaches None) and the impact (a hang) all match the label.
